column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
“Make strong” retains the verb applied to Pharaoh’s heart rather than “harden.”
The heart of Pharaoh and his servants is turned, retaining the heart image and passive wording rather than their changing their minds.
Says Pharaoh harnessed his chariot and took his people, rather than merely prepared the chariot and took his army.
Calls the six hundred chariots chosen, rather than the best, and does not explicitly add “other” before all the chariots of Egypt.
“With a raised hand” retains the bodily image rendered “defiantly.”
Speaks of Pharaoh’s chariot horses rather than listing horses and chariots as separate items.
Retains “lifted their eyes” and repeats the Israelites as the subject of crying out.
